criteria.no: The item does not state the directive: it is silent about it, names only the topic, or describes a different approach.
criteria.unclear: The item states part of the directive's content but it cannot be determined whether it plans the directive itself.
criteria.yes: The item says sanity-stack's claim has a timeout, that on expiry it reports the holder, and that dev-sanity then keeps the task active and retries.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires that sanity-stack takes a timeout for the stack bead claim and on expiry returns the holder's identity, claim time and active task, and dev-sanity then keeps the sanity task active, asks the holder once, continues other sanity work and retries, with no refusal, no FAIL to the dev and no escalation to a person. Does `item.text` state this directive's specific content as a step, constraint or decision? An item that only names the topic, or that waits without limit, refuses the task, fails the dev or asks a person, does not state it. Judge presence of the directive only, not whether the item conflicts with it.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item is one of the ruled-out cases, including when the item is silent about the directive.
criteria.unclear: The item is ambiguous enough that it might describe one of the ruled-out cases, but it cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: The item states a plan, approach or decision that is one of the ruled-out cases.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan something that `anchor.statement` rules out? The anchor rules out: waiting on the claim with no time limit; refusing or closing the sanity task because the lock is busy; sending the dev a FAIL because of the lock; escalating to a person about the lock, for example messaging Rand, the user or a human operator. These are not a conflict: silence about the lock timeout; messaging the lock holder once; claiming and releasing the stack bead around a write. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.

anchor.statement: sanity-stack must take a timeout for the stack bead claim, and on expiry must return the holder's identity, claim time and active task; dev-sanity must then keep the sanity task active, ask the holder once, continue other sanity work and retry; neither may refuse the task, fail the dev or escalate to a person.
anchor.scope: sanity-stack input timeout_s (default 60, retry 5 s), its lock_timeout result, dev-sanity's handling, the stack bead lease

item.text: dev-sanity closes the sanity task refused because the lock was busy, or sends the dev a FAIL, or sends the user a message asking who holds the lock.
